title: fix(app-shell): decide the permission matrix's artifact tier by ADR-0010 provenance (objectui#4526)
body:
Fixes #4526
Clause-②: no

This PR implements item 2 of the maintainer-adopted triage ruling on objectui#4526 (comment 5814482093, 「第⑧批 同意」). It was done under the `domain:ui` seat 1 claim 5824875998, on branch `claude/issue-4526-matrix-artifact-by-provenance`, in session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`. The same ruling accepts item 1 (the single-kernel over-lock) as known behaviour. This PR records that in the docblock and adds no environment probe.

## What changed

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`: `isArtifactBackedLayer` now checks the layered envelope's ADR-0010 `provenance` as well as the `sys_metadata` sentinel: `code != null && code._packageId !== 'sys_metadata' && provenance !== 'org'`. That is the same source and the same clauses `ResourceEditPage` uses for `isArtifactItem`.
  - The input type widens structurally to `{ code?: unknown; provenance?: unknown }`. The call site already passes the whole `MetadataLayered` envelope, so the line that feeds it is unchanged.
  - No export, fetch or `useMetadataClient` signature changes.
- The docblock is rewritten. It explains the two exclusions and why each one is there. It says that an `undefined` provenance keeps the artifact reading. It adds a section that records the single-kernel over-lock as accepted behaviour, with its restart condition: a new card once the client has a legitimate read of the kernel's environment topology.
- Two comments described the same decision and now name both clauses: the ARTIFACT-tier block above `artifactTierApplies`, and the load effect's comment where the predicate is fed. The first one had a cross-file line address into `ResourceEditPage`. The rewritten sentence names the file instead.
- `PermissionMatrixEditor.artifactTier.test.tsx`: the fake client can now serve `provenance`, and a new describe block adds four pins (listed below). The 12 existing cases are unchanged and still serve no `provenance`, so they now also pin the "no opinion" path.
- `.changeset/4526-matrix-artifact-by-provenance.md`: `minor` for `@object-ui/app-shell`, because this changes behaviour for tenant sets.

## Mechanism assumptions, measured (dispatch zone 2)

1. **Holds.** On base `9ec8ceba0` the predicate was `code._packageId !== 'sys_metadata'` alone. The load effect fed it through `setCodeIsArtifact(isArtifactBackedLayer(lay))`, and its docblock said to adopt provenance when this card was picked up.
2. **Holds.** `ResourceEditPage` computes `isArtifactItem` inline as `!createMode && layered?.code != null && code._packageId !== 'sys_metadata' && layered?.provenance !== 'org'`. It reads `provenance` off the layered envelope (`MetadataLayered.provenance`, the body of `GET /meta/:type/:name/layers`).
   - No shared helper exists for the envelope form. `isPackagedFlowItem` in `views/setup/packagedFlows.ts` reads the item-level `_provenance` key, which is a different source.
   - So the clauses are mirrored inline, and the comment points to the sibling by symbol.
3. **Holds.** The envelope this editor already fetches (`client.layered(type, name)`) is a `MetadataLayered`. It declares `provenance`, and `MetadataClient.layered` forwards it on both the schema-valid path and the degrade path. No new fetch is needed.
4. **Same decision.** The "three-way rule" block computes `artifactTierApplies`, `canWriteByType` and `lockedByArtifactTier` from `codeIsArtifact`, which is the predicate's output. The code there therefore moves with the predicate. Only its comment still said "the same `sys_metadata` sentinel", and this PR updates that comment.

Server side, read for context only on the objectstack checkout at `c1641868` (not changed here): the envelope's `provenance` is resolved from `code ?? overlay`. The registry's artifact lookup excludes both the sentinel and tenant-authored items (`isTenantAuthored`). The client now mirrors both exclusions.

## Pins

The new block runs everything at environment scope (no `packageId`), with the stock `permission` flags (`allowOrgOverride: false`, `allowRuntimeCreate: true`) unless a case says otherwise.

- **(a)** A tenant's own set, `provenance: 'org'`, with a sentinel `code` layer, is editable: Save is enabled, the checkbox is enabled, there is no lock badge and no artifact caption.
- **(c)** A tenant's own set rehydrated under a real package id (`_packageId: 'com.example.showcase'`, `provenance: 'org'`) is editable, including the row's bulk buttons. The old predicate got this case wrong.
- **(b)** A code-declared set (`provenance: 'package'`, real package id) is read-only. There is no Save, every checkbox is disabled, and the artifact caption is shown.
- **(b')** The same set is writable when the type allows overlay (`allowOrgOverride: true`).

The existing case "code-declared set at environment scope is READ-ONLY" serves no `provenance`, so it also pins that a server which sends no provenance still gets the artifact reading.

## Reverse proof

I ran this on the committed change (`f85eaf512`), through the objectstack `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. It replaced the clause `layered?.provenance !== 'org'` with `true`, which restores the old sentinel-only predicate.

- **On disk:** anchor count went from 1 to 0, marker count from 0 to 1, and the blob from `7718307acfa5` to `0cf2e14683f0`.
- **Result:** `Tests 1 failed | 15 passed (16)`. The one failure is pin (c), "a tenant's own set rehydrated under a REAL package id (provenance 'org') is EDITABLE", with `Unable to find an accessible element with the role "button" and name /^Save$/`. It went red, as predicted.
- Pin (a) stays green, because the sentinel already covers it. It is a positive control, not the pin that proves the change.
- **Restore:** the blob is back to `7718307acfa5`, equal to HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- The suite imports the component from source by relative path, so no build runs between the mutation and the test run.

## Gates (all at `f85eaf512`)

- **Build:** `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2` finished 28 of 28 tasks successfully.
- **Type-check:** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exits 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists both touched files.
- **metadata-admin tests:** `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` from the repo root gives `Test Files 292 passed (292)` and `Tests 3159 passed | 1 skipped`.
- **Whole `packages/app-shell/`:** I ran it in four shards so each one fits the ten-minute cap. It covered 776 files (775 passed, 1 skipped) and 7665 tests passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed.
- **Tests and gates that read the touched sources as text:** `permission-slice.authoredKeys.test.ts` and `CelPredicateField.labelBinding.test.tsx` ran in the metadata-admin run. These gates read `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` or its test by name, and all exit 0: `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:installed-pin-claims`.
- **Named repo gates:**
  - `pnpm check:control-bytes`: OK.
  - `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `0 new citation(s)`.
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: the changeset is present.
  - `pnpm check:changeset-claims`: nothing to re-read.
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: OK.
- **ESLint** over the two touched files, HEAD against base (base read via `--stdin`), counted by rule and severity:
  - The counts are identical at HEAD and base. The editor has 18 `no-explicit-any`, 1 `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` and 1 `react-hooks/refs`. The test has 2 `no-explicit-any`. All of them are warnings.
  - Type-aware linting is not configured (`eslint.config.js` has no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`), so this diff cannot change the verdict on any other file.

## Does item 2 fire on a real deployment? (the `?package=` question)

This is a source reading, not a live measurement, and it changes the question.

- On the metadata-admin route (`metadata/:type/:name`), `MetadataResourceEditPage` passes a registered custom editor only `type` and `name` (`Custom type={type} name={name}`). The registry types that slot as a `ComponentType` of `{ type: string; name: string }`.
- `PermissionMatrixEditPage` does not read the query string.
- So on that route this editor always runs at the environment door, whether or not the list link carries `?package=`. (`ResourceListPage` does append `?package=` when an active package is set.) Only the Studio Access pillar passes `packageId`.

So item 2 does not depend on the link. It depends only on one thing: whether a live server serves a tenant-authored permission set with a real `_packageId` on its `code` layer. That is the rehydration shape cloud#970 measured for other types, but I did not measure it for `permission` on a running deployment.

`NOT MEASURED: live deployment reachability, reason: no environment probe or live stack was in scope for this card.`

## Acceptance notes

- **Two copies remain.** `ResourceEditPage` and this editor now agree clause for clause but still spell the predicate separately. A shared helper would need a new export, and this dispatch ruled that out.
- **Stale cross-file line addresses remain** in comments this PR did not touch: the TYPE-gate comment in `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`, and the header and the fail-open case of `PermissionMatrixEditor.artifactTier.test.tsx`. I left them alone to stay inside the file surface the claim declared.
- **The custom-editor dispatch drops `?package=`,** as described above. This PR does not answer whether the permission matrix on the metadata-admin route should honour the active package; that is a product question. Carrier: none.
- **No docs change was needed:** `packages/app-shell/README.md` and `content/docs` do not describe the artifact tier's predicate.
